name: Integrated Heat Spreader (IHS)
definition: A thermally conductive metallic lid mounted atop the silicon die and sealed to the package substrate to protect the die and distribute concentrated thermal energy across a larger contact area.
primaryFunction: Conduct heat away from fragile silicon die hotspots toward an external heatsink or cold plate while providing mechanical protection against mounting pressure.
engineeringPrinciples: Fourier's Law of heat conduction (q = -k grad T); reducing thermal interface resistance by spreading high power density (W/mm^2) over a wider surface area.
construction: Stamped or forged oxygen-free copper body electroplated with nickel for oxidation resistance and solderability, bonded via Thermal Interface Material (TIM) above the die.
operation: Thermal energy generated by switching transistors propagates vertically through the silicon bulk and TIM into the IHS base, spreads laterally across the copper plate, and transfers to an external cooler.
outputs: Distributed heat flux into external thermal solution
Clamping load routed around die edges to pkg-substrate

relationships.description: Encloses and thermally cools the silicon die via TIM.
Perimeter bonding skirt seals directly onto the package substrate.
Spreads concentrated thermal hotspots from core execution logic.

realWorldContext: Used across desktop, workstation, and server socketed LGA processors to prevent die cracking under heavy cooler retention forces.

name: Silicon Die (Physical Die Carrier)
definition: A thin rectangular block of high-purity monocrystalline silicon diced from a semiconductor wafer onto which the processor's integrated circuits are fabricated.
primaryFunction: Serve as the physical semiconductor substrate housing billions of nanoscale CMOS transistors and multi-layer metal interconnects.
engineeringPrinciples: Photolithographic patterning of doped silicon channels (FEOL) and back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper/cobalt metal interconnect stacks.
construction: Crystalline silicon wafer slice thinned to hundreds of micrometers, topped with active transistor layer and 10-15+ metal routing layers terminating in flip-chip bump pads.
operation: Provides electrical semiconductor junctions for switching logic and routes signals and power rails from package bumps to internal core and cache regions.
inputs: Regulated VDD/VSS power rails and I/O signals via pkg-solder-bumps
outputs: Processed external signals
Thermal energy upward into pkg-ihs

relationships.description: Transfers die heat upward through TIM into the IHS lid.
Mounted onto area-array C4 solder bumps.
Houses the functional CPU core floorplan regions.

realWorldContext: Monolithic and chiplet dies in modern desktop CPUs, mobile SoCs, and data-center accelerators.

name: Package Substrate
definition: A multi-layer miniature printed circuit interposer that bridges the ultra-fine-pitch micro-connections of the silicon die to the macro-scale pads facing the motherboard socket.
primaryFunction: Fan out dense die I/O and power connections while maintaining signal integrity, controlled impedance, and mechanical rigidity.
engineeringPrinciples: High-density interconnect (HDI) multi-layer routing, micro-via fan-out, ground/power reference planes, and decoupling capacitor mounting.
construction: Core laminate (glass-reinforced resin with ABF build-up films) containing 8-16+ copper signal and power planes connected by laser-drilled micro-vias.
operation: Routes differential high-speed I/O lanes and distributed power rails radially outward from central flip-chip bump pads to bottom-side electrical contacts.
internalStructure: Bottom contact pad grid & SMD decoupling caps
inputs: Power and external signals from pkg-electrical-contacts
outputs: Impedance-matched signals and low-inductance power to pkg-solder-bumps

relationships.description: Bottom surface carries gold LGA contact pads.
Feeds regulated power and signals upward through C4 bumps.
Supports perimeter mechanical seal of the IHS.

realWorldContext: Organic flip-chip BGA/LGA substrates used across workstation, desktop, and server CPUs.

name: Solder Bumps (C4 Array)
definition: Microscopic spherical metallic interconnect joints arranged in an array beneath a flip-chip silicon die that electrically and mechanically bond the die to the package substrate.
primaryFunction: Deliver ultra-high-density power, ground, and I/O connections directly across the entire area of the die face rather than only its perimeter.
engineeringPrinciples: Controlled Collapse Chip Connection (C4 / flip-chip) area-array bonding reduces parasitic inductance and IR voltage drop compared with peripheral wire-bonding.
construction: Lead-free tin-silver-copper (SAC) solder spheres or copper-pillar micro-bumps reflowed onto UBM pads, surrounded by capillary epoxy underfill.
operation: Thousands of parallel bump columns carry high-amperage core supply directly above active logic blocks while signal bumps pass high-frequency data into substrate micro-vias.
inputs: Bidirectional I/O and DC power from pkg-substrate
outputs: Power and signal rails into pkg-silicon-die

relationships.description: Electrically and mechanically bonds directly under the die.
Reflowed onto top HDI pads of the package substrate.
Routes DDR PHY pins toward substrate traces.

realWorldContext: Flip-chip processors, 2.5D/3D stacked dies, and high-bandwidth package assemblies.

name: Electrical Contacts (LGA Pad Array)
definition: The macroscopic array of gold-plated contact pads (LGA), pins (PGA), or solder balls (BGA) on the underside of the CPU package substrate that mate with a motherboard socket.
primaryFunction: Provide a reliable, serviceable electromechanical interface connecting the processor package to system power delivery, clock inputs, DRAM channels, and PCIe/I/O lanes.
engineeringPrinciples: Contact resistance minimization via gold-over-nickel plating, differential pair assignment with ground shielding, and mechanical compliance under socket spring tension.
construction: Precision array of electroplated copper/nickel/gold flat LGA pads arranged around a central cavity for bottom-side decoupling capacitors.
operation: Spring-loaded socket pins press against each contact pad, completing parallel electrical pathways for VRM power, reference clocks, memory channels, and system I/O.
inputs: Motherboard VRM power, reference clock, resets, DRAM/PCIe signals
outputs: Memory requests, I/O transactions, thermal telemetry to motherboard

relationships.description: Forms the bottom external interface of the package substrate.
Carries external DRAM channel signals to the motherboard.
Receives external reference crystal clock input.

realWorldContext: Land Grid Array (LGA) sockets on desktop and server motherboards; BGA balls on mobile platforms.

name: CPU Cores Array (Die Floorplan Region)
definition: The partitioned silicon floorplan zones dedicated to independent instruction-executing processor cores replicated across the die.
primaryFunction: Provide parallel hardware execution engines capable of fetching, decoding, and executing independent instruction streams concurrently.
engineeringPrinciples: Thread-level parallelism (TLP) via chip multiprocessing (CMP); trading single-thread frequency scaling limits for replicated power-efficient cores.
construction: Symmetric rectangular floorplan tiles containing front-end fetch/decode, execution core subsystems, and private L1/L2 SRAM caches.
operation: Each core operates an independent Program Counter and execution pipeline while sharing coherent access to last-level cache and memory over the die interconnect.
inputs: Instructions and data from L2/L3 cache and interrupts
outputs: Memory read/write transactions and computed state updates

relationships.description: Fabricated onto the active FEOL layer of the silicon die.
Each core tile houses processing-core subsystems including the ALU.
Exchanges cache lines and coherence messages via ring/mesh stops.

realWorldContext: Multi-core desktop, laptop, and cloud server microprocessors.

name: Cache Regions (Shared LLC Floorplan)
definition: Dedicated high-density SRAM array zones across the silicon die housing private L2 and shared L3 (Last-Level Cache) storage banks.
primaryFunction: Bridge the latency and bandwidth gap between high-speed core execution units and slower off-die system DRAM.
engineeringPrinciples: Spatial and temporal locality; dense 6-transistor (6T) SRAM bitcells tiled into uniform sub-arrays with tag comparators and ECC protection.
construction: Highly regular rectangular SRAM macro arrays often occupying 30%-50%+ of total die area, divided into slices distributed along the interconnect fabric.
operation: Core cache misses propagate to distributed L3 slices hashed by physical address; hits return cache lines over the interconnect without crossing off-die pins.
inputs: Core cache miss requests and coherence probes
outputs: Cached lines back to cores or miss requests to die-memory-controller

relationships.description: Occupies large SRAM floorplan banks on the silicon die.
Physical floorplan counterpart to mem-l3-cache.
Connected to all cores via sliced interconnect stops.

realWorldContext: Sliced Last-Level Cache (LLC) architectures in desktop and server CPUs.

name: Execution Units Cluster (Die Floorplan)
definition: The silicon area within each processor core tile dedicated to integer arithmetic, floating-point, SIMD/vector, and address generation hardware datapaths.
primaryFunction: Concentrate the highest switching-activity logic circuits responsible for actual arithmetic and bitwise computation on the die.
engineeringPrinciples: Bit-sliced datapath regularity for minimal wire delay; high thermal power density requiring optimal placement relative to the IHS.
construction: Tightly packed standard-cell and custom datapath macros arranged beside register file read/write ports to minimize signal propagation delay.
operation: Receives decoded micro-operations and operand values from register read ports, computes outputs within clock cycles, and forwards results onto write-back buses.
inputs: Decoded control vectors and register operands
outputs: Computed results, condition flags, and memory effective addresses

relationships.description: Inset computational cluster inside each CPU core tile.
Macro floorplan view of core-execution-units.
Primary hotspot region cooled through TIM and IHS.

realWorldContext: Integer/SIMD datapath clusters in modern out-of-order superscalar processors.

name: Die Interconnect Fabric
definition: The high-bandwidth on-die communication fabric (ring bus, 2D mesh, or crossbar Network-on-Chip) linking CPU cores, cache slices, memory controllers, and I/O blocks.
primaryFunction: Transport cache lines, coherence messages, and I/O traffic deterministically and without deadlock across all on-die functional regions.
engineeringPrinciples: Packet-switched or multi-stop ring/mesh routing; cache coherence protocol messaging; bisection bandwidth scaling with core count.
construction: Wide multi-layer upper BEOL metal routing buses interspersed with buffered router switches at every core and cache slice.
operation: When a core or I/O agent initiates a memory transaction, packetized address/data flits traverse hop-by-hop across interconnect stops to the target slice or controller.
inputs: Read/write requests, coherence snoops, DMA traffic
outputs: Routed packets to die-cache-regions, die-memory-controller, or die-io-controller

relationships.description: Links all 4 core tiles together.
Connects cores to shared L3 cache slices.
Physical floorplan spine for comm-interconnect-network.

realWorldContext: Ring interconnects in desktop CPUs and 2D mesh NoCs in high-core-count server processors.

name: Integrated Memory Controller (IMC)
definition: The on-die hardware subsystem that translates internal CPU cache-line read/write requests into external DRAM physical timing and protocol commands.
primaryFunction: Manage communication with off-die main memory (DRAM), scheduling read/write queues, row activations, precharges, and periodic refresh cycles.
engineeringPrinciples: Out-of-order memory scheduling (FR-FCFS) to maximize open-row hits, bank-level parallelism, ECC support, and DDR PHY serialization.
construction: Digital transaction scheduler logic coupled to mixed-signal DDR PHY I/O buffers located along the perimeter edge of the silicon die.
operation: On an L3 miss, maps physical address to channel/rank/bank/row/column, asserts DRAM timing commands within JEDEC specs, and returns data to the interconnect.
outputs: Electrical DDR signals out through pkg-solder-bumps and pkg-substrate

relationships.description: Receives off-die memory transactions from the interconnect.
Hardware implementation backing mem-main-interface.
Routes DRAM channel pins directly out through edge bumps.

parameters.label: Die Location
parameters.value: Perimeter edge for short I/O routing

realWorldContext: Integrated DDR4/DDR5/LPDDR5 memory controllers embedded directly on modern CPUs and SoCs.

name: I/O Controller
definition: On-die interface blocks managing high-speed external peripheral communication protocols such as PCIe lanes, DMA engines, display links, and platform buses.
primaryFunction: Enable high-throughput Direct Memory Access (DMA) and peripheral communication between the CPU complex and storage, networking, GPUs, and chipset devices.
engineeringPrinciples: Packetized serial differential signaling (SerDes), credit-based flow control, IOMMU address translation, and interrupt routing.
construction: Digital protocol transaction and link layers adjacent to high-speed analog SerDes transceiver lanes placed near die edges.
operation: Serializes internal parallel packets onto differential PCIe/I/O lanes, arbitrates DMA transfers into coherent memory, and delivers interrupts to cores.
inputs: Peripheral DMA requests, device interrupts, MMIO writes
outputs: Memory-mapped transactions to die-interconnect
High-speed serial signals via pkg-solder-bumps

relationships.description: Streams coherent DMA traffic onto the die interconnect.
Exposes differential PCIe/I/O lanes at socket pads.

realWorldContext: Integrated PCIe root complexes, USB/Thunderbolt host controllers, and SoC I/O hubs.

name: Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
definition: The combinational digital logic circuit inside a processing core that performs integer arithmetic (ADD, SUB, MUL) and bitwise logical operations (AND, OR, XOR), while emitting processor status flags.
primaryFunction: Execute computational operations on register operands and evaluate comparison conditions driving program control flow.
engineeringPrinciples: Two's complement binary arithmetic, Boolean algebra, carry-lookahead/parallel-prefix addition, and multiplexer output selection.
construction: Bit-sliced combinational logic network built from adders, logic gate arrays, shifters, and output selector multiplexers.
operation: Receives two source operands (OpA, OpB) and ALUOp from core-control-unit, computes output within one cycle, and updates Z, N, C, V status flags.
outputs: Computed 32-bit result to WRITE_BACK / LSU
Updated FLAGS (Z, N, C, V)

relationships.description: Centerpiece computational unit inside core-execution-units.
Steered by ALUOp control assertions.
Built conceptually from combinational binary adders and MUXes.

realWorldContext: Every scalar integer pipeline inside x86, ARM, RISC-V, and embedded microcontroller cores.

name: Control Unit (CU)
definition: The supervisory sequential and combinational logic unit that orchestrates instruction sequencing and drives the control signals governing every datapath component across execution stages.
primaryFunction: Coordinate fetch, decode, register read, ALU operation selection, memory read/write enabling, PC increment/branching, and register write-back timing.
engineeringPrinciples: Finite State Machine (FSM) stage sequencing (hardwired control logic or microcoded ROM control) with synchronous clock-edge coordination.
construction: Combinational decode PLA/logic arrays paired with sequential stage state flip-flops distributing control wires across the core.
operation: Tracks current stage (FETCH..WRITE_BACK), reads decoded opcode and FLAGS, and asserts deterministic control signals (RegWrite, MemRead, MemWrite, ALUOp, PCWrite) per cycle.
outputs: comm-control-signals driving registers, ALU, LSU, and PC

relationships.description: Consumes decoded opcode and operand fields.
Asserts ALUOp function code during EXECUTE.
Originates all warm-gold control signal assertions.

realWorldContext: Hardwired RISC control pipelines and hybrid microcode sequencers in CISC processors.

name: Registers (Architectural Core State)
definition: The smallest, fastest on-core data storage elements directly named by processor instructions and internal execution control state.
primaryFunction: Hold active operands, intermediate arithmetic values, instruction pointer (PC), current instruction (IR), memory interface buffers (MAR/MDR), and condition flags (FLAGS).
engineeringPrinciples: Zero-cycle-overhead synchronous SRAM/flip-flop latching with direct dual-read / single-write port topology.
construction: 8 general-purpose 32-bit registers (R0-R7) plus dedicated control/interface registers (PC, IR, MAR, MDR, FLAGS).
operation: During REGISTER_READ, source indices drive OpA/OpB onto ALU buses; during WRITE_BACK, rising clock edges latch destination Rd when RegWrite = 1.
outputs: Dual read operand buses (OpA, OpB)
Current PC value

relationships.description: Architectural view of the physical mem-register-file SRAM array.
Supplies OpA and OpB operands and captures write-back results.
Implemented synchronously using edge-triggered flip-flops.

realWorldContext: Architectural register files in RISC-V, ARM, and x86-64 (backed internally by larger physical rename files).

name: Instruction Decoder
definition: Combinational decode logic that extracts the opcode, register specifiers, immediate constants, and addressing mode from the fetched instruction word in IR.
primaryFunction: Translate structured instruction representations into explicit control vectors and operand identifiers required by downstream execution units.
engineeringPrinciples: Fixed-field opcode decoding (characteristic of RISC/educational ISAs) vs. variable-length parsing; combinational bit-field slicing.
construction: Combinational gate logic wired to IR output lines, feeding core-control-unit and core-registers read-select inputs.
operation: Reads instruction latched during FETCH, extracts opcode (LOAD, ADD, STORE, JMP, etc.), identifies Ra, Rb, Rd, and passes decoded fields to the Control Unit.
outputs: Parsed opcode class, register indices, immediate literal to core-control-unit

relationships.description: Receives fetched instruction words directly from L1i.
Feeds decoded opcode vector into Control Unit.
Implemented as stateless combinational decode logic.

realWorldContext: Front-end instruction decoders (single-cycle in fixed-width RISC vs. multi-stage predecode/uop-cache in x86 CISC).

name: Execution Units (Core Subsystem)
definition: The collective execution functional units inside a single core encompassing integer ALUs, multipliers, branch evaluation units, and shifter datapaths.
primaryFunction: Perform diverse instruction computations in specialized functional lanes once operands arrive from the register file.
engineeringPrinciples: Functional unit specialization (separating fast 1-cycle integer addition from multiplication or branch evaluation) and issue dispatch.
construction: Partitioned functional blocks grouped behind operand multiplexers and connected to shared result write-back buses.
operation: Dispatches decoded operation type to the matching functional subunit (core-alu integer/logic, multiplier, or branch target evaluator).
outputs: Computation output, updated FLAGS, branch target resolution

relationships.description: Encompasses core-alu as its primary integer/logic lane.
Core-level view of die-execution-units floorplan block.
Hands effective addresses and store operands to LSU.

realWorldContext: Superscalar multi-port execution engines enabling IPC > 1 on modern desktop and server cores.

name: Load/Store Unit (LSU)
definition: The dedicated core subsystem responsible for calculating memory addresses and executing memory read (LOAD [addr] / LOADM) and memory write (STORE) transactions.
primaryFunction: Decouple memory addressing and data-cache/memory bus handshakes from arithmetic ALU operations.
engineeringPrinciples: Load/store architecture discipline, memory bounds verification (0..255), and MAR/MDR interface buffering.
construction: Bounds checker and address generation logic coupled to MAR, MDR, and mem-l1-dcache / comm-memory-interface ports.
operation: During MEMORY_ACCESS, latches target address into MAR; on LOAD [addr] reads MEM[MAR] into MDR; on STORE writes Rs via MDR into MEM[MAR].
outputs: Loaded data to WRITE_BACK
Memory bus transactions to mem-l1-dcache / comm-memory-interface

relationships.description: Directly interfaces with L1 Data Cache during MEMORY_ACCESS.
Drives MAR/MDR handshake across memory interface.
Gated by MemRead and MemWrite control lines.

realWorldContext: Load/store queues and memory disambiguation hardware in RISC and out-of-order superscalar processors.

name: L1 Instruction Cache (L1i)
definition: The fastest, core-private instruction-only SRAM cache directly feeding the core's front-end fetch logic.
primaryFunction: Supply instructions every clock cycle without suffering main memory stalls or data-traffic contention.
engineeringPrinciples: Split Harvard L1 cache organization (separating instruction fetches from data accesses) and spatial/temporal instruction locality.
construction: Small, ultra-low-latency SRAM tag + instruction word arrays located immediately adjacent to core-instruction-decoder.
operation: During FETCH, receives PC, looks up matching instruction slot, and delivers the instruction to IR; on miss, requests fill from mem-l2-cache.
outputs: Fetched instruction word to core-instruction-decoder (IR)

relationships.description: Feeds fetched instructions straight into IR and decoder.
Backed by unified L2 cache on instruction misses.
Split Harvard counterpart to L1 Data Cache.

realWorldContext: Split L1 instruction caches in modern x86, ARM, and RISC-V cores.

name: L1 Data Cache (L1d)
definition: The fastest, core-private data-only SRAM cache directly attached to the Load/Store Unit for operand loads and stores.
primaryFunction: Provide single-digit-cycle read/write caching for frequently accessed program variables, stacks, and array elements.
engineeringPrinciples: Set-associative lookup, write-back vs. write-through policies, spatial locality via cache lines, and conflict avoidance vs. L1i.
construction: Low-latency multi-banked SRAM array supporting parallel tag comparison adjacent to core-load-store-unit.
operation: On LOAD [addr] or STORE, checks tag match; hits resolve directly inside L1d while misses propagate outward to mem-l2-cache.
inputs: Memory address (MAR) and store data (MDR) from core-load-store-unit
outputs: Loaded word to MDR / WRITE_BACK
Miss/writeback lines to mem-l2-cache

relationships.description: Directly services LSU load and store requests.
Sends misses and dirty evictions to unified L2 cache.
Split Harvard counterpart to L1 Instruction Cache.

realWorldContext: Core-private L1 data caches across general-purpose desktop, mobile, and server processors.

name: L2 Cache
definition: The unified secondary SRAM cache level (holding both instructions and data) sitting between core-private L1 caches and the shared L3 cache.
primaryFunction: Capture L1 instruction and data misses quickly with substantially larger capacity than L1, shielding cores from slower L3 and DRAM latencies.
engineeringPrinciples: Unified cache organization, higher associativity to lower conflict misses, and inclusion/non-inclusion coherence management.
construction: Medium-density 6T SRAM array integrated per core tile, visibly larger than L1i and L1d.
operation: Services miss requests from both L1i and L1d; returns cached lines on hit or forwards misses onto die-interconnect toward mem-l3-cache.
inputs: L1 miss fills and writebacks from mem-l1-icache and mem-l1-dcache
outputs: Cache lines to L1
Miss/snoop messages to mem-l3-cache

relationships.description: Services instruction misses from L1i.
Services data misses from L1d.
Backed by shared Last-Level Cache slices.

realWorldContext: Private per-core L2 caches in modern desktop/mobile cores or cluster-shared L2 in efficiency cores.

name: L3 Cache (Last-Level Cache)
definition: The large, die-wide shared Last-Level Cache (LLC) shared across multiple processor cores to hold shared code/data and accelerate inter-core communication.
primaryFunction: Minimize expensive off-die DRAM accesses and serve as the central coherence point across all cores on the die.
engineeringPrinciples: Distributed sliced SRAM banks connected via die-interconnect, directory/snoop-filter coherence tracking, and high capacity density.
construction: High-density SRAM bank arrays organized into slices corresponding to die-cache-regions, occupying major silicon surface area.
operation: Receives L2 miss transactions over die-interconnect, hashes target address to owning slice, resolves shared data hits or escalates misses to mem-main-interface.
outputs: Cache lines to requesting core
DRAM fill/writeback requests to mem-main-interface

relationships.description: Logical memory-hierarchy view of die-cache-regions.
Backs private L2 caches across all cores.
Escalates LLC misses to main DRAM interface.

realWorldContext: Shared Last-Level Cache (LLC) and 3D-stacked cache expansions in desktop and data-center CPUs.

name: Register File (Memory Hierarchy Tier 0)
definition: The multi-ported SRAM/flip-flop storage array forming the apex (Tier 0) of the CPU memory hierarchy, directly addressable by instruction register fields.
primaryFunction: Deliver multiple simultaneous operand reads and result writes within the processor core's clock cycle at minimal energy per access.
engineeringPrinciples: Multi-port bitcell design (2R1W: two read ports, one write port per cycle), fixed short 3-bit index addressing (R0-R7), zero tag comparison overhead.
construction: Tightly pitched array of multi-ported register bitcells wired directly to wordlines/bitlines and core-alu operand buses.
operation: Decoded Ra/Rb indices activate parallel read wordlines during REGISTER_READ to emit operands simultaneously; Rd write wordline activates during WRITE_BACK.
outputs: Parallel operand streams (OpA, OpB) to core-execution-units

relationships.description: Physical hierarchy tier corresponding to core-registers.
Constructed from clocked flip-flops / multi-port SRAM cells.
Sits above L1 caches at the apex of the memory pyramid.

realWorldContext: Integer and vector register files inside every CPU and GPU streaming core.

name: Main Memory Interface
definition: The hierarchical boundary connecting on-die last-level cache through the Integrated Memory Controller to external system DRAM.
primaryFunction: Provide high-capacity working system memory storage when data and instructions exceed on-die cache capacity.
engineeringPrinciples: Latency vs. capacity trade-off (1T1C DRAM density vs. 6T SRAM speed) and burst cache-line transfers over external DDR channels.
construction: Logical abstraction encompassing the die-memory-controller interface, comm-memory-interface bus channels, and off-package DRAM boundary.
operation: When L3 misses (or on direct educational memory steps), sends read/write address and burst command out of the chip package to external DRAM arrays.
inputs: Cache-line fill or dirty writeback requests from mem-l3-cache / LSU
outputs: Data words back to mem-l1-dcache / MDR

relationships.description: Physical controller driving external DDR memory pins.
Internal MAR/MDR bus bridge leading to DRAM.
Backs L3 Last-Level Cache on off-die misses.

realWorldContext: System DDR4/DDR5/HBM memory subsystem boundary in desktop, mobile, and server computers.

name: Transistors (MOSFET / FinFET Conceptual Model)
definition: Microscopic semiconductor field-effect switches (CMOS NMOS and PMOS pairs) whose gate voltage controls current flow between source and drain terminals.
primaryFunction: Act as ultra-fast, solid-state voltage-controlled switches representing binary 0 (VSS) and 1 (VDD).
engineeringPrinciples: Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) operation: NMOS pulls outputs low when gate is HIGH; PMOS pulls outputs high when gate is LOW; dynamic power P = alpha * C * V^2 * f.
construction: Enlarged conceptual 3D FinFET/MOSFET cross-section showing silicon substrate, doped source/drain regions, vertical fin channel, high-k gate oxide, and gate electrode.
operation: Applying threshold voltage to the gate forms a conductive inversion channel between source and drain; removing gate voltage pinches off conduction.
outputs: Switched drain/source logic level (0 or 1)

relationships.description: Fundamental switching primitive composing all Boolean logic gates.
Billions of nanoscale transistors reside on the active FEOL silicon layer.

realWorldContext: Billions of FinFET and Gate-All-Around (GAAFET) CMOS transistors integrated per processor die.
scaleDisclaimer: CONCEPTUAL MODEL — NOT TO SCALE: Enlarged didactic circuit model illustrating switching and Boolean logic concepts. Real silicon transistors operate at nanometer scales.

name: Logic Gates
definition: Elementary CMOS transistor circuits implementing Boolean algebraic functions (NOT, NAND, NOR, AND, OR, XOR) over binary voltage inputs.
primaryFunction: Transform discrete binary input signals into deterministic Boolean output signals, forming the building blocks of all digital computation.
engineeringPrinciples: Boolean algebra, functional completeness (NAND/NOR universality), noise margins, and complementary pull-up (PMOS) / pull-down (NMOS) networks.
construction: Conceptual 3D circuit module depicting CMOS transistor pairs alongside standard Boolean gate blocks (AND, OR, XOR, NOT).
operation: Input combinations turn specific PMOS/NMOS paths ON or OFF so the output connects cleanly to either VDD (1) or VSS (0) with minimal static current.
outputs: Deterministic Boolean truth-table output (Y in {0, 1})

relationships.description: Constructed from complementary NMOS and PMOS transistors.
XOR, AND, and OR gates compose half and full adders.
Gate arrays implement selector multiplexers.

realWorldContext: Standard-cell libraries used across synthesis of every digital ASIC and microprocessor core.
scaleDisclaimer: CONCEPTUAL MODEL — NOT TO SCALE: Enlarged didactic circuit model illustrating switching and Boolean logic concepts. Real silicon transistors operate at nanometer scales.

name: Flip-Flops (Edge-Triggered Storage)
definition: Bistable sequential logic elements (primarily rising-edge-triggered D-Flip-Flops) that sample an input bit on a clock edge and hold it stable across the entire clock period.
primaryFunction: Store binary state reliably between combinational logic stages, enabling registers, counters, pipeline latches, and FSM memory.
engineeringPrinciples: Cross-coupled bistable feedback loops (Master-Slave D-latches), setup time (t_setup), hold time (t_hold), and clock-to-Q propagation delay (t_pcq).
construction: Enlarged conceptual 3D module showing paired Master and Slave D-latches controlled by complementary clock phases (CLK, ~CLK).
operation: While CLK = 0, the master latch tracks input D while the slave holds Q. On the rising clock edge (0 -> 1), master freezes and slave presents the new Q.
outputs: Stored bit Q and complement ~Q

relationships.description: Built from cross-coupled CMOS logic gates.
Provides synchronous state storage inside sequential circuits.
Sampled synchronously on rising CLK edges.

realWorldContext: Pipeline registers, program counters, status flags, and hardware state machines in every synchronous CPU.
scaleDisclaimer: CONCEPTUAL MODEL — NOT TO SCALE: Enlarged didactic circuit model illustrating switching and Boolean logic concepts. Real silicon transistors operate at nanometer scales.

name: Multiplexers (MUX Data Selectors)
definition: Combinational selector circuits that route one of 2^N binary data inputs onto a single output line under the control of an N-bit select signal.
primaryFunction: Implement hardware data routing, operand selection, register port selection, ALU output picking, and PC next-address selection (PC+1 vs. branch target).
engineeringPrinciples: Sum-of-products decoding of select signals combined with AND-OR gating or CMOS transmission gates.
construction: Enlarged conceptual trapezoid selector assembly with visible In0..In3 rails, Sel control lines, and gated active path to Out.
operation: Binary select bits enable exactly one input channel path while isolating all others, steering the chosen signal combinational-style to the output.
outputs: Selected single data stream (Y)

relationships.description: Constructed from combinational AND/OR or transmission gates.
Selects ALU inputs and output lanes.
Steers datapath branches under Control Unit direction.

realWorldContext: Datapath routing, bypass/forwarding networks, and register file read-port selection in every CPU.
scaleDisclaimer: CONCEPTUAL MODEL — NOT TO SCALE: Enlarged didactic circuit model illustrating switching and Boolean logic concepts. Real silicon transistors operate at nanometer scales.

name: Adders (Half, Full & Fast Adders)
definition: Combinational arithmetic circuits built from XOR, AND, and OR gates that compute the binary sum and carry-out of two binary operands.
primaryFunction: Form the arithmetic heart of core-alu for addition, subtraction (two's complement A + ~B + 1), address calculation, and PC incrementing.
engineeringPrinciples: Half-adder (S = A XOR B, C_out = A*B), Full-adder with carry-in, and fast parallel-prefix carry-lookahead trees overcoming ripple-carry delay.
construction: Enlarged modular Full-Adder slice stacked into a multi-bit carry-chain visual model showing Sum and Carry lanes.
operation: Propagates sum bits through XOR trees while computing carry generate and propagate terms across bit positions.
internalStructure: Overflow XOR comparator (V = C_n-1 XOR C_n)
outputs: Binary Sum
Carry-out (C_out)
Signed Overflow flag (V)

relationships.description: Built from XOR, AND, and OR combinational gates.
Core arithmetic kernel inside core-alu.
Stateless combinational arithmetic circuit.

parameters.label: Carry-Lookahead Delay

realWorldContext: 32/64-bit integer ALUs, address generation units (AGUs), and floating-point mantissa adders.

name: Combinational Circuits
definition: Stateless digital logic networks whose outputs depend strictly and deterministically on the current combination of inputs after combinational propagation delay.
primaryFunction: Execute decoding, multiplexing, shifting, comparison, and arithmetic transformations between clocked storage boundaries.
engineeringPrinciples: Memoryless Boolean mapping Y = f(X), acyclic signal topology (no feedback loops), and worst-case critical propagation delay (t_pd).
construction: Conceptual multi-layer acyclic gate fabric showing signal flow strictly from input pins through logic layers to output pins.
operation: Whenever inputs change, logic states cascade forward across gate layers until settling to stable output values prior to the next rising clock edge.
outputs: Settled logic results ready for latching by logic-sequential

relationships.description: Composed purely of acyclic interconnected logic gates.
Feeds settled outputs into clocked sequential flip-flops.
Underpins stateless instruction decoding.

realWorldContext: Instruction decode PLAs, ALU datapaths, barrel shifters, and cache tag comparators.
scaleDisclaimer: CONCEPTUAL MODEL — NOT TO SCALE: Enlarged didactic circuit model illustrating switching and Boolean logic concepts. Real silicon transistors operate at nanometer scales.

name: Sequential Circuits
definition: State-retaining digital circuits combining combinational logic with clocked memory elements (logic-flip-flops) so outputs depend on both current inputs and stored history.
primaryFunction: Implement finite state machines (FSMs), counters (PC), registers, and synchronized pipeline stages that step cleanly across clock cycles.
engineeringPrinciples: Synchronous state machine theory (Mealy and Moore FSM models), next-state feedback loops gated by flip-flops, and timing closure.
construction: Conceptual feedback-loop assembly pairing a combinational next-state cloud with a clocked flip-flop state register bank.
operation: Combinational next-state logic computes the upcoming state from current state + inputs; on the rising clock edge, flip-flops capture the new state atomically.
outputs: Updated state vector and synchronous control/data outputs

relationships.description: Uses clocked flip-flops to retain state across cycles.
Pairs combinational next-state logic with storage latches.
Implements the 6-stage Control Unit FSM.

realWorldContext: Control unit FSMs, branch history tables, counters, and synchronous pipeline stage registers.
scaleDisclaimer: CONCEPTUAL MODEL — NOT TO SCALE: Enlarged didactic circuit model illustrating switching and Boolean logic concepts. Real silicon transistors operate at nanometer scales.

name: Internal Buses
definition: Shared parallel sets of electrical signal conductors inside the processor carrying addresses, data payloads, and control attributes between functional blocks.
primaryFunction: Provide organized multi-bit transport channels separating addressing (Address Bus), payload transport (Data Bus), and coordination (Control Bus).
engineeringPrinciples: Multiplexed bus arbitration, parallel bit-width bandwidth (BW = W * f_bus), and bus contention prevention.
construction: Color-coded multi-rail conductor pathways spanning across core-*, mem-*, and comm-memory-interface in the 3D scene.
operation: During each stage, core-control-unit grants bus ownership to one active driver (e.g., PC onto Address Bus in FETCH, ALU onto Writeback Bus in WRITE_BACK).
internalStructure: Data bus rails (IR / MDR / OpA / OpB / WB)
inputs: Driven outputs from registers, caches, ALU, or LSU
outputs: Delivered words and addresses to targeted destinations

relationships.description: Transports addresses and operands to/from registers.
Feeds dual operands into the ALU.
Structural bus rails carrying datapath packets.

realWorldContext: Internal processor core buses and AMBA/AXI SoC bus fabrics.

name: Data Paths
definition: The complete directional flow network of registers, multiplexers, buses, and execution units through which instruction operands and results travel during execution.
primaryFunction: Define the physical and logical routes data follows across every step of the FETCH -> DECODE -> REGISTER_READ -> EXECUTE -> MEMORY_ACCESS -> WRITE_BACK cycle.
engineeringPrinciples: Datapath vs. Control separation (datapaths carry operands/results; control unit selects MUX paths and latch enables).
construction: Directed topological graph of spline segments (edgeId) linking L1i -> Decoder -> Registers -> ALU -> LSU -> Registers.
operation: On every simulated cycle, CpuSnapshot.activePaths specifies active datapath edges, triggering luminous cyan packet flow between exact source and destination components.
inputs: Active stage and opcode semantics from core-control-unit
outputs: Synchronized operand delivery and visual packet trajectory vectors

relationships.description: Routes operands into ALU and results out to WB/LSU.
Originates reads and terminates write-backs.
Carries memory addresses and words to/from LSU.

realWorldContext: Processor datapath microarchitecture blueprints in RISC and superscalar cores.

name: Control Signals
definition: Dedicated binary and multi-bit command wires asserted by core-control-unit to instruct every datapath component how to behave on a given clock cycle.
primaryFunction: Synchronize multiplexers, register write-enables (RegWrite), memory enables (MemRead, MemWrite), ALU function selectors (ALUOp), and PC updates.
engineeringPrinciples: Hardwired combinational control decoding and visual separation of data planes (cyan) from control assertions (warm gold).
construction: Fine radiating filament overlays connecting core-control-unit directly to MUXes, register write ports, ALU mode inputs, and LSU pins.
operation: At the onset of each stage, core-control-unit drives exact signal tuples (e.g., ALUOp=ADD, RegWrite=1) reflected live in 3D filaments and simulator telemetry.
inputs: Decoded opcode and FLAGS into core-control-unit
outputs: Synchronized control signals into all core-* and comm-data-paths MUXes

relationships.description: Asserted directly by the Control Unit each cycle.
Selects active ALU arithmetic/logic operation.
Gates register file write-back via RegWrite.

realWorldContext: Pipeline control buses inside microprocessor control paths.

name: Clock Distribution
definition: The synchronized timing network (PLL clock generator + balanced H-tree / resonant clock mesh) delivering uniform periodic clock pulses across the entire silicon die.
primaryFunction: Coordinate state transitions across millions of sequential elements (flip-flops, registers, pipeline latches) with minimal clock skew.
engineeringPrinciples: Equal wire-length balanced H-tree topology minimizing skew (delta t_skew), clock gating for power savings, and PLL frequency synthesis.
construction: Symmetrical fractal H-tree metallic conductor overlay branching evenly across die-cpu-cores and core stage registers.
operation: Every rising clock tick synchronously latches updated state across core-control-unit, core-registers, and sequential barriers.
outputs: Phase-aligned CLK timing edges across all sequential subsystems

relationships.description: Synchronizes rising-edge sampling of sequential flip-flops.
Advances stage FSM transitions on each clock cycle.
Branches symmetrically across all 4 CPU core tiles.

realWorldContext: Balanced H-tree, spine-and-rib, and resonant clock grids in high-frequency desktop and server CPUs.

name: Interconnect Network
definition: The high-level logical topology connecting cores, shared caches, memory controllers, and I/O blocks into one coherent multiprocessor fabric.
primaryFunction: Enable scalable parallel data exchange and cache coherence traffic across multi-core and heterogeneous die subsystems without point-to-point wiring explosion.
engineeringPrinciples: Ring vs. 2D Mesh vs. Crossbar NoC topologies; hop latency vs. bisection bandwidth trade-offs; packet switching with virtual channels.
construction: Bidirectional multi-ring or 2D grid overlay mapped directly onto die-interconnect, featuring router switch nodes at every core and LLC slice intersection.
operation: Encapsulates core cache misses, coherence probes, and DMA requests into routed flits traversing switches from source stop to target stop.
inputs: Coherent memory/snoop requests from die-cpu-cores and die-io-controller
outputs: Routed transactions to target mem-l3-cache slices or die-memory-controller

relationships.description: Logical signal topology overlay matching die-interconnect.
Exchanges coherent messages among all 4 cores.
Routes cache-miss requests to sliced L3 banks.

realWorldContext: Multi-core ring interconnects, 2D mesh NoCs, and die-to-die chiplet fabrics.

name: Memory Interface (Bus & Protocol Bridge)
definition: The internal-to-external memory transaction interface bridging core-load-store-unit (MAR/MDR) and L1 caches onto die-memory-controller and external mem-main-interface.
primaryFunction: Serialize memory read/write requests, buffer addresses and data payloads (MAR/MDR), and decouple synchronous core timing from off-core memory response latencies.
engineeringPrinciples: Address/data/control handshaking (Req/Ack), Memory Address Register (MAR) & Memory Data Register (MDR) buffering.
construction: Explicit MAR/MDR interface latches plus dual-directional address and data conduits connecting core LSU/L1 boundary to die-memory-controller.
operation: Receives target address into MAR and outbound data into MDR (for STORE); asserts MemRead or MemWrite; returns retrieved word into MDR for WRITE_BACK.
inputs: Address, data, and MemRead/MemWrite controls from LSU / CU
outputs: Memory channel request to die-memory-controller / mem-main-interface

relationships.description: Receives memory transaction requests from LSU.
Forwards off-core transactions to the IMC.
Logical bus bridge backing main memory accesses.

realWorldContext: Bus Interface Units (BIUs) and cache-to-memory controller transaction bridges.
